independentAuthorityFindings.candidate: Texas Comptroller PTAD Property Value Study, live pages at comptroller.texas.gov/auto-data/PT2/PVS/, fetched 2026-09-09
independentAuthorityFindings.independentBecause: Published directly by the state agency with statutory oversight (Tax Code 5.10/5.102), not by Hays CAD or this program.
independentAuthorityFindings.whatWasFound: The 2024P index for Hays (105index.php) confirms PTAD conducts a full stratified study across all 7 Hays-area ISDs, with per-category/per-district Confidence Interval and Stratified Ratio detail pages. One directly fetched (Dripping Springs ISD, 105-904, 2023 Confidence Interval Detail) shows genuine per-category parcel totals in the low thousands (category A alone: 3,103-3,620), the correct order of magnitude for that district's slice of the county roll. PTAD's own site does not publish a single rolled-up all-category, all-district grand total on one page -- the total has to be assembled ISD-by-ISD, category-by-category, which is exactly what Hays CAD's Annual Report states it did ('based on the 2025 Comptroller's Audit Reports').
independentAuthorityFindings.limitation_honestlyStated: I did not personally re-sum all 7 ISDs x ~12 categories from PTAD's own worksheet pages to independently reconstruct 132,358 from raw Comptroller data -- the per-ISD Summary Worksheet tables render client-side (present in the WebFetch-rendered read, absent from the raw HTML a plain curl retrieves), and re-deriving 84 individual category-cells was judged not worth the marginal confidence gain given the strength of the corroboration already in hand (see next section). This is named as a real gap in this lane's own rigor, not glossed over.

whyTheCorroborationIsStrongDespiteTheGap: Two numbers from two different tables in the SAME Hays CAD document, produced by two different internal processes (budget/accounts tracking vs. Comptroller-audit-sourced category count), land within 180 of each other (132,538 vs 132,358) -- if either were fabricated or mislabeled, this close an agreement between two unrelated internal processes would be a coincidence.

Neither number is anywhere near 172,116 (the padded 2025 comparator) -- both are within 1% of the prior lane's already-established 131,246 'CAD-only 2025' figure, and within 1.7% of our own 134,606 2026 ingest, on the LOW side (both PRECEDE our 2026 figure and are smaller than it, consistent with one more year of normal growth, not consistent with a roll that's supposed to be 172K).
This report was published 2025-12, five months before our 2026-07-16 ingest and independent of it in time as well as in pipeline.

perCapitaSanityCheck.note: Explicitly weak per the dispatch's own framing (item 4) -- reported as weak, not leaned on.
perCapitaSanityCheck.populationSources: Hays: Hays CAD's own 2025 Annual Report, 'approximately 309,000-312,000 residents' (2025 est., Census Bureau-sourced per the report). Travis/Williamson/Caldwell: 2025 Census Bureau county population estimates via web search, figures 1,363,767 / 752,827 / 55,150 respectively.

residentsPerAccount_2025or2026roll.Hays: ~310,500 / 134,606 = 2.31 (using 2026 roll against 2025 population est., the closest available pairing)
residentsPerAccount_2025or2026roll.Caldwell: 55,150 / 48,382 = 1.14 (rural, land-parcel-heavy roll -- expected to run low)

perCapitaSanityCheck.reading: Hays sits inside the Travis-Williamson band, not below it. If Hays were genuinely missing 30,000+ accounts (true count ~164,600), its ratio would drop to ~1.89 -- noticeably below Williamson's suburban 2.36 and closer to rural Caldwell's shape, which would be an odd fit for a county whose growth profile (per the Annual Report) is suburban/exurban, not rural. This is weak, directional corroboration for reading 2, not proof.

preRegisteredFalsifier_outcome.recap: Stated in CP1 before any fetch: near-or-below ~134,600 (121,000-148,000 band) confirms reading 2; near 172,000+ reopens mechanism A and fires the falsifier.
preRegisteredFalsifier_outcome.actualIndependentFigures: 132,358 and 132,538 (Hays CAD's own 2025 Annual Report, one branch attributed to Comptroller Audit Reports) -- both inside the confirming band, both on the low-and-growing side of our 134,606, neither anywhere near 172,000.
preRegisteredFalsifier_outcome.fired: NO. Reading 2 is confirmed by a source outside this program's fetch/parse/store pipeline.

midWorkAdversarialCheck.question: Could the Annual Report's numbers themselves be circular -- e.g., did Hays CAD just copy our own bulk-export total into their annual report, making this a false independent check?
midWorkAdversarialCheck.reasoning: No plausible path for that: the Annual Report's 132,358/132,538 are 2025-tax-year figures, published 2025-12, seven months before our program's first 2026 ingest (2026-07-16) and eight-plus months before this lane's 2026-09-09 read. Hays CAD cannot have copied a number our program produced later. The 132,358 branch is explicitly attributed to the Comptroller, an entirely separate compiling authority. The two branches also come from different report sections (budget/operations vs. reappraisal-plan/Comptroller-citation) prepared for different purposes.
midWorkAdversarialCheck.conclusion: The independence holds on timing and on authorship grounds. No basis to discount it.

decision: Reading 2 confirmed by an authority outside this program's own pipeline. Falsifier did not fire. Mechanism A stays closed. No re-acquire, no apply, no gate change. Proceeding to close.
